properties.title: The Boone family moves to Upper Louisiana
properties.description: Daniel and Rebecca Boone moved with family members to Spanish Upper Louisiana. Daniel received land in the Femme Osage area but often stayed with his children; the interpreted stone home here was Nathan Boone’s later residence.
properties.locationAccuracy: The Final Move interpretive marker at the Historic Daniel Boone Home. This later Nathan Boone house interprets the family’s move; it is not Daniel’s 1799 land-grant footprint.
properties.locationBasis: The Final Move interpretive marker at the Historic Daniel Boone Home. This later Nathan Boone house interprets the family’s move; it is not Daniel’s 1799 land-grant footprint.
properties.source: St. Charles County Parks
properties.coordinateEvidence: HMDB marker: 38°39.107′ N, 90°51.192′ W; 1868 Highway F.

properties.title: St. Charles Borromeo church is dedicated

properties.title: Clark’s campaign brings Cahokia under American control
properties.description: George Rogers Clark’s Illinois campaign gained control of Cahokia, then a British-held post with a French population. Joseph Bowman’s headquarters became known as Fort Bowman, placing the village within the western theater of the American Revolution.
properties.locationAccuracy: Fort Bowman marker at Cahokia Wedge; the original headquarters stood east of the church and no longer survives.
properties.locationBasis: Fort Bowman marker at Cahokia Wedge; the original headquarters stood east of the church and no longer survives.
properties.source: National Park Service
properties.coordinateEvidence: HMDB Fort Bowman marker: 38°34.247′ N, 90°11.286′ W.

properties.title: A French timber residence becomes a lasting landmark
properties.description: The building later used as Cahokia Courthouse began as a French colonial home. Upright timbers resting on a horizontal sill illustrate the post-on-sill building method brought to the Mississippi Valley.
properties.locationAccuracy: Interpretive marker on the original courthouse site. The present structure incorporates surviving fabric after removal and reconstruction.
properties.locationBasis: Interpretive marker on the original courthouse site. The present structure incorporates surviving fabric after removal and reconstruction.
properties.source: Illinois Department of Natural Resources
properties.coordinateEvidence: HMDB marker: 38°34.232′ N, 90°11.541′ W; official Illinois site confirms 107 Elm Street.

properties.title: Indigenous leaders meet Clark at Cahokia
properties.description: Clark convened a council with Indigenous leaders to seek peace and weaken British alliances. Some leaders accepted an agreement while others retained their British ties; the gathering did not represent a single choice by all Native nations.
properties.locationAccuracy: Public Cahokia Wedge reference point for the council held in the village; no exact council seating or gathering boundary is claimed.
properties.locationBasis: Public Cahokia Wedge reference point for the council held in the village; no exact council seating or gathering boundary is claimed.
properties.source: National Park Service
properties.coordinateEvidence: HMDB Cahokia marker at Wedge: 38°34.254′ N, 90°11.332′ W.

properties.title: A French mission takes root at Cahokia
properties.description: Missionaries from Quebec established the Mission of the Holy Family beside existing Indigenous communities. The French village of Cahokia grew around the mission; it is distinct from the much older Mississippian city near Collinsville.
properties.locationAccuracy: Marker at the surviving late-18th-century Holy Family church; earlier mission structures should not be assumed to share its exact footprint.
properties.locationBasis: Marker at the surviving late-18th-century Holy Family church; earlier mission structures should not be assumed to share its exact footprint.
properties.source: Illinois Department of Natural Resources
properties.coordinateEvidence: HMDB marker on church front: 38°34.221′ N, 90°11.283′ W; 116 Church Street.

properties.title: Cahokia Illini settlement and chapel at Monks Mound
properties.description: After conflict over French settlement and land, Cahokia Illini moved to the Monks Mound area. A French mission chapel stood on the first terrace. Archaeology and written records document this later Indigenous occupation, centuries after the Mississippian city.
properties.locationAccuracy: Public interpretive marker on the Monks Mound approach; not an exact archaeological excavation or building footprint.
